description: No venue satisfies every soft preference. The two hard constraints still fully determine the answer; the rest is an agreed, defensible compromise rather than a computed optimum.

expected.reasoning: Meshek Barzilay is known to violate Adi's kosher requirement, so the hard-constraint filter eliminates it regardless of rating — that part is mechanical. Between the two remaining kosher, vegan-friendly options, Nanuchka Kosher is better-rated but HaKosem Kerem is the only one an actual stated participant preference (Hila's modest budget) points toward; nobody stated a preference for a higher-rated or pricier venue. Agreed by the team on this basis. HaKosem closes at 22:30 while the group is free until 23:00, and that shortens the evening rather than ruling the venue out: the slot is the intersection, 19:30-22:30. This scenario is the clearest case of that rule — the answer that survives is the venue that closes earliest of the three. The group's window was 20:30-23:00 until the three-hour minimum meeting length was agreed; it starts at 19:30 so that HaKosem's shortened evening still clears the minimum.
